question: isometrics for mid portion Achilles pain
search_summary: Searched PubMed/Europe PMC via web search, PEDro, BJSM and JOSPT guidelines, Cochrane: Achilles tendinopathy/tendinosis AND isometric/static hold/heavy isometric, plus loading guidelines. About 40 records screened.

pico.p: Adults with mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy, early stage
pico.i: Isometric calf loading (e.g. 5 x 45 s heavy holds)
pico.c: Isotonic, eccentric or HSR calf loading, or no exercise
pico.o: Pain (immediate and short term), VISA-A, return to activity

suggestions.title: Achilles Pain, Stiffness, and Muscle Power Deficits: Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy Revision – 2024
suggestions.citation: Chimenti RL, Neville C, Houck J, Cuddeford T, Carreira D, Martin RL. Achilles Pain, Stiffness, and Muscle Power Deficits: Midportion Achilles Tendinopathy Revision – 2024. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2024.
suggestions.why: Current US physio guideline for mid-portion Achilles; states where isometrics sit in loading recommendations.

suggestions.title: Dutch multidisciplinary guideline on Achilles tendinopathy
suggestions.citation: de Vos RJ, van der Vlist AC, Zwerver J, Meuffels DE, Smithuis F, van Ingen R, et al. Dutch multidisciplinary guideline on Achilles tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med 2021;55(20):1125-34.
suggestions.why: Pain- and fatigue-guided progression of calf loading for 12+ weeks; doesn't single out isometrics.

suggestions.title: Effectiveness of isometric exercise in the management of tendinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials
suggestions.citation: Clifford C, Challoumas D, Paul L, Syme G, Millar NL. Effectiveness of isometric exercise in the management of tendinopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials. BMJ Open Sport Exerc Med 2020;6(1):e000760.
suggestions.why: Only review dedicated to isometrics across tendinopathies; 10 RCTs, isometrics not superior to isotonic.

suggestions.title: Isometric exercises do not provide immediate pain relief in Achilles tendinopathy: a quasi-randomized clinical trial
suggestions.citation: van der Vlist AC, van Veldhoven PLJ, van Oosterom RF, Verhaar JAN, de Vos RJ. Isometric exercises do not provide immediate pain relief in Achilles tendinopathy: a quasi-randomized clinical trial. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2020;30(9):1712-21.
suggestions.why: Only controlled Achilles test of isometric vs isotonic for immediate pain; complements O'Neill 2019 in your library.

suggestions.title: Eccentric and isometric exercises in Achilles tendinopathy evaluated by the VISA-A score and shear wave elastography
suggestions.citation: Gatz M, Betsch M, Dirrichs T, Schrading S, Tingart M, Michalik R, Quack V. Eccentric and isometric exercises in Achilles tendinopathy evaluated by the VISA-A score and shear wave elastography. Sports Health 2020;12(4):373-81.
suggestions.why: Only Achilles RCT with an isometric arm over weeks; isometrics added to eccentrics, PEDro 5/10.

suggestions.title: Which treatment is most effective for patients with Achilles tendinopathy? A living systematic review with network meta-analysis of 29 randomised controlled trials
suggestions.citation: van der Vlist AC, Winters M, Weir A, Ardern CL, Welton NJ, Caldwell DM, et al. Which treatment is most effective for patients with Achilles tendinopathy? A living systematic review with network meta-analysis of 29 randomised controlled trials. Br J Sports Med 2020.
suggestions.why: Network meta-analysis: no active treatment clearly best; supports starting with any calf loading programme.

suggestions.title: Heavy slow resistance versus eccentric training as treatment for Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled trial
suggestions.citation: Beyer R, Kongsgaard M, Hougs Kjaer B, Ohlenschlaeger T, Kjaer M, Magnusson SP. Heavy slow resistance versus eccentric training as treatment for Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled trial. Am J Sports Med 2015;43(7):1704-11.
suggestions.why: Mid-stage alternative: HSR vs eccentrics with 52-week follow-up; the dosing template many use after isometrics.

suggestions.key: continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study
suggestions.title: Continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study
suggestions.citation: Silbernagel KG, Thomeé R, Eriksson BI, Karlsson J. Continued sports activity, using a pain-monitoring model, during rehabilitation in patients with Achilles tendinopathy: a randomized controlled study. Am J Sports Med 2007;35(6):897-906.
suggestions.why: Source of the pain-monitoring model for early-stage load and activity decisions; PEDro 8/10.

suggestions.title: Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy
suggestions.citation: Rio E, Kidgell D, Purdam C, Gaida J, Moseley GL, Pearce AJ, Cook J. Isometric exercise induces analgesia and reduces inhibition in patellar tendinopathy. Br J Sports Med 2015;49(19):1277-83.
suggestions.why: Origin of the isometric-analgesia claim: 6 volleyballers, patellar tendon; Achilles studies haven't reproduced it.

gaps: No RCT tests isometrics as an early-stage loading programme over weeks in mid-portion Achilles.
Immediate-analgesia data in Achilles come from small uncontrolled or quasi-randomised studies.
Trials recruit chronic cases (over 3 months); early, reactive or highly irritable presentations are barely studied.
No Achilles isometric data in in-season athletes or high-load sports.

answer.answer: Don't rely on calf isometrics for pain relief in early mid-portion Achilles: the one checked direct study found no immediate drop. Use them, if at all, as tolerable starting load, then progress. Evidence is very thin.
actions: Don't promise immediate pain relief from calf isometrics.
If a reactive tendon tolerates nothing else, start 5 x 45 s holds daily at tolerable load.
Judge loading on next-morning pain and stiffness, not on an immediate hop retest.
Keep pain during loading at or below 4/10, settled within 24 hours.
Progress to isotonic heel raises, then heavy calf loading, as pain allows.
Don't add isometrics to an eccentric programme expecting extra VISA-A gains.

comparison.title: Heavy 45-s calf isometrics: no immediate pain relief
comparison.finding: Functional pain 4.2 to 4.9/10 after 5 x 45 s holds; CI excludes a 2-point drop

comparison.title: Load progression criteria in lower limb tendinopathy
comparison.finding: One Achilles isometric trial: adding isometrics to eccentrics, VISA-A change 23% vs 20%

comparison.title: Criteria-gated Achilles rehab protocol
comparison.finding: Isometrics as entry rung (5 x 45 s daily if calf-raise pain >5/10); no results yet

comparison.title: Protocol: eccentrics versus controls review
comparison.finding: No data; isometrics only an eligible comparator

comparison.title: Pole vaulter insertional Achilles case (conference abstract)
comparison.finding: Isometrics in weeks 1–2, undosed, within a package; VISA-A +20 at 4 months

comparison.title: Calcific patellar tendinopathy case
comparison.finding: Isometrics in weeks 1–2 within a four-part package; indirect to Achilles

agreement: Neither direct Achilles study shows isometrics add pain relief or function over other loading.
Protocols and cases place isometrics only as a short entry stage before isotonic loading.
conflicts: Rio's patellar analgesia result isn't reproduced in the Achilles: older, chronic runners and a different tendon.
No checked study tests isometrics over weeks as the early-stage programme itself.
